rationale: DEEP_RESEARCH_FINDINGS.v001 section 5: PLAYLIST traffic = 19.6 min/view, 10x any other source, on 1.1% of views. Suggested traffic is 100% borrowed adjacency. Playlists + end screens are the only levers that manufacture our OWN co-watch edges. R-26 asked for 4 series playlists covering all long-forms.
ordering_rule: Position 1 = highest measured reach x watch-through in the cluster (it is the video the playlist link lands on). Then escalate the stakes rather than follow publish date, keep the two weakest-APV videos out of positions 1-3, and place the weakest last so a broken session ends late rather than early.
end_screen_rule: slot 1 = the NEXT video in this playlist; for the last position, slot 1 = position 1 (loops the session back to the entry point). slot 2 = this playlist.
deviations_from_research: The research named the 4th cluster 'Unsolved & Disaster'. 5 of its 8 members are wrongful convictions or institutional betrayal, not unsolved cases, so it is renamed 'The System Got It Wrong'. A viewer who clicks an unsolved-mystery label and lands on an exoneration film bounces; the rename protects the 19.6 min/view.
The research counted 40 long-forms. The true census is 42 - the uploads playlist omits bYcqabvvxak (Terry, 2026-06-21) and Qyad4FejCIc (Hinton, 2026-07-14). Both are assigned here.

P3 reuses the existing 'Fraud, Finance & Power' playlist and P1 reuses 'Landmark Rights Cases' rather than creating new ones, because 4 live descriptions already link those two ids. Creating replacements would strand those links.

playlists.title: Police Power: What They Can Actually Do to You
playlists.description:
A traffic stop. A phone in your pocket. A knock at the wrong door. Every film here is one real case that decided how far the police can go before they need a warrant - and what happens to the person who found out the hard way. Watch in order: the cases build from the roadside to your front door to the interrogation room.

New case every week.

playlists.title: The Forfeiture Files: When the Government Takes What's Yours
playlists.description:
Nobody was convicted of anything. The house, the car, the savings, the surplus from the sale - taken anyway, legally. These are the real cases behind civil forfeiture, tax-sale windfalls and eminent domain, and the ordinary people who spent years getting their own property back.

Watch in order - the amounts get smaller and the injustice gets sharper.
playlists.entry_point_reason: 172 views - the highest of any long-form on the channel - and the premise (following the rule is what made her a target) is the cluster's cleanest stakes gap.

order.note: eminent domain - the widest frame, closes the arc

playlists.title: Fraud, Finance & Power
playlists.description:
Nine real collapses: the money that was never there, the warnings nobody acted on, and the people who were paid enormously to look away. Ponzi schemes, fake technology, a trillion dollars that vanished in 36 minutes, and the fine print that quietly took your right to sue.

Watch in order - each film explains the machinery the next one runs on.
playlists.entry_point_reason: 57 views at 19.13% APV - the best combination in this cluster, and the whistleblower framing is the cluster's strongest present-tense injustice.

playlists.title: The System Got It Wrong
playlists.description:
Eight cases the system never answered for: men who spent decades in prison for crimes they did not commit, a judge who was paid by the jail he sent children to, evidence that stayed buried, and disappearances still open after fifty years.

Watch in order - the wrongful convictions first, then the cases nobody ever closed.
